notes: The temporary test tests/unit/features/zzAudit.report.test.js was created, run and deleted, and no repo files were changed. Lesser findings left out: businessHistory turns 'resigns amid SEC probe' into career; Karim Atiyeh's Form D roles are not shown; screensOf caps cites at 6; dateWindows chaining; r9 #85 is mis-dated (title says 2026, dated 2024). Saved reports strip score, so I re-derived the ranking in tests.

findings.title: Relatives and co-founders of OTHER people are pinned on the founder
findings.scenario: Text 'Trevor Milton sued Ford CEO Jim Farley and his brother John Farley, chairman of Acme Holdings' gives relative John Farley, 'brother', role chairman. 'Ford founder Henry Ford and co-founder Jim Smith spoke' gives associate Jim Smith as Milton's co-founder. Both become trusted threads, are searched with the founder and are listed under Related parties.
findings.fix: Relatives: accept his/her/their only when the nearest preceding person name or pronoun antecedent in the sentence is the subject (no other full name between the subject and the kin word). Co-founder: run the ofAnother test on the nearest preceding proper noun, skipping 'and', so '<Org> founder X and co-founder Y' counts as another company's.
findings.evidence: Temporary jest run: relativesFromText returned John Farley as brother/chairman; associatesFromText returned Jim Smith 'named as a co-founder'.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. relativesFromText returned John Farley (brother, chairman) from 'his brother' that refers to Jim Farley. associatesFromText added Jim Smith: the ofAnother lead regex needs a capitalised word right before 'co-founder', and 'Henry Ford and ' ends in 'and', so the check never runs.
findings.betterFix: For his/her/their kin, reject the match when plausiblePerson finds a full name between the subject's last mention (or the sentence start) and the possessive. For co-founder, strip a trailing 'and' or comma before running the lead regex, and treat '<Org> founder <Name> and co-founder' as another company's. Add both sentences as regression tests.

findings.title: Second reader's made-up role makes any company it mentions a fully checked 'own' company
findings.scenario: A confirmed record names Milton and also says 'Ford CEO Jim Farley announced a recall'. The model proposes {company:'Ford', role:'co-founder'}. verifyGaps keeps it as trusted thread 'co-founder; named in a record about the person (News)', and tieOf() returns 'primary'. Ford is then checked in full, and its lawsuits and recalls land as records about 'a company they founded or run'.
findings.fix: Check companies the way people are checked: the role words (PRIMARY_TIE) must be in a sentence that names both the subject and the company, otherwise keep the thread with role '' and the why 'named with the person'. That makes it an affiliate. Never copy x.role into why unless it appears in that sentence.
findings.evidence: Jest repro: verifyGaps kept Ford with why 'co-founder; named in a record...', and tieOf gave 'primary'.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. verifyGaps kept Ford with why 'co-founder; named in a record...' only because the record names Milton somewhere. tieOf returned 'primary', so Ford gets a full check and its matters are filed as the person's company. Nothing checks the role against a sentence that names the subject.

findings.title: Associates from the second reader need no sentence that names the founder
findings.scenario: For the same record, the model proposes Jim Farley with tie 'business'. tieIn finds 'CEO' in Farley's sentence, which never names Milton, and returns 'stated'. Farley becomes a trusted associate: screened, searched together with Milton and shown under Related parties. This contradicts the file header's rule that the tie must be in a sentence naming the person.
findings.fix: In tieIn, count TIE_WORDS only when the same sentence also matches subject.hasName, or opens with a pronoun that continues a sentence naming the subject (reuse sentencesAbout from extract.js). Add a regression test with two sentences.
findings.evidence: Jest repro: threads included {kind:'associate', value:'Jim Farley', trusted:true}.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. tieIn tests TIE_WORDS only on the sentence that contains the proposed name ('Ford CEO Jim Farley announced a recall'), which never names Milton. Jim Farley became a trusted associate. The 'kin' path in publicRelativeIn has the same gap: it never requires the subject in the sentence.
findings.betterFix: Count a tie only in a sentence that names the subject, or a pronoun sentence that continues one (export sentencesAbout from extract.js), and require the tie word within roughly 60 characters of the proposed name. Apply the same subject-sentence rule to the kin path through publicRelativeIn.

findings.title: 'Claims that changed' lists other people's bios and marketing-copy edits
findings.scenario: In r9 Glyman, #37 is the bio of 'Stefanie', a content marketer, on a ramp.com blog page. It is graded confirmed and shown as his claim change. #19, #21, #30 and #33 are product-copy and podcast blurb rewrites, as are #4 and #8 in r8 (Shensi Ding). Only #1, #8, #105 and #109 are real claim changes.
findings.fix: Keep a change only when the before or after text names the subject (or opens with a pronoun on the subject's own profile page) and the difference touches a claim token: a title, employer, school, degree or year. Put the other changes in the archive section only, never in claimChanges or the brief.
findings.evidence: r9 claimChanges: n=37 with quote 'Prior to Ramp, Stefanie worked as a finance reporter...', and n=21 with 'Easy-to-use cards, funds, approval flows...'.
findings.verifyNote: report.js line 632 keeps every archive 'change' record that is not 'possible'. archive.js builds bio and headline diffs from whole pages, including company blog pages with several people, and grades a change by the page's match. Nothing checks that the changed text is about the subject. I could not re-check the r9 data myself, but the code allows exactly what the finding describes.
findings.betterFix: Fix this at the source, in archive.js when the change finding is built. For a page that is not the person's own profile, keep a bio or headline change only when its before or after text names the subject. Mark marketing-copy diffs as info and keep them out of claimChanges. The report filter can then also require field in role, title, education or headline, or a bio diff that names the subject.

findings.title: 'Screens with no match' claims clean for screens that waited out, partly answered, or never ran fully
findings.scenario: Sanctions ran 1 lookup and waited out 4; UK Gazette returned partial=['notices']. screensOf marks both 'partial', but cleanScreens lists both under 'Screens with no match' in the brief and in the model's prompt. SCREENS also lacks the delaware-courts, eu-courts, canada-federal-courts, us-bank-regulators, fincen-actions, leak-sites and breach-catalogue ids, so real clean screens go unstated (as in the r9 brief).
findings.fix: Build cleanScreens from screensOf output: status === 'clear' only, with labels from SCREEN_GROUPS and source labels. Delete the separate SCREENS map and the stale 'bodacc' and 'icij' ids. Add waitedOut and partial to coverage.searched rows.
findings.evidence: Jest repro: screens sanctions-lists:partial and uk-gazette:partial, yet cleanScreens returned ['sanctions (US, UN, EU, UK, Canada)','UK Gazette notices'].
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. screensOf marked sanctions (4 lookups waited out) and uk-gazette (partial) as 'partial', yet cleanScreens returned both as 'Screens with no match', because coverage.searched carries neither waitedOut nor partial. SCREENS also lacks delaware-courts, eu-courts, canada-federal-courts, us-bank-regulators, fincen-actions, leak-sites and breach-catalogue. This breaks rule 5 (honest coverage).

findings.title: Related party shown as 'screened' when its watchlist lookup failed or waited out
findings.scenario: The sanctions lookup for associate Karim Atiyeh fails with HTTP 503. deepCheck still pushes the task key into state.done (failed and waited-out tasks stay in `ran`), and buildReport marks him screened:true. Screens by mdb-debarment, us-bank-regulators and fincen-actions never count, because WATCHLISTS omits them.
findings.fix: In deepCheck, record failed and waited-out task keys (state.failed) and remove them from done, or record succeeded screens explicitly. The report sets screened only from succeeded watchlist tasks and lists the screens that failed for each party. Add mdb-debarment, us-bank-regulators and fincen-actions to WATCHLISTS.
findings.evidence: Jest repro: sources errors=1 of runs=1 and done=['sanctions-lists|associate|Karim Atiyeh|screen'] gave relatedParties[0].screened === true.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. A us-exclusions lookup for an associate that failed with HTTP 503 still produced screened:true. In deepCheck.js, failed and waited-out tasks stay in `ran` and go into state.done; only retried or rested tasks are removed. WATCHLISTS also omits mdb-debarment, us-bank-regulators and fincen-actions.
findings.betterFix: In deepCheck, add the task key to state.screenedOk only when a watchlist task returns a result, and keep failed or waited-out keys in state.screenFailed. The report then sets screened from screenedOk and lists the screens that failed for each party. Do not take failed keys out of done, because done also prevents re-queueing.

findings.title: Sanctions, debarment and wanted-list red flags sort below a resignation
findings.scenario: A confirmed high-severity World Bank debarment (category sanctions, source mdb-debarment) and a medium 'Trevor Milton resigns as chairman' press item are both red flags. flagWeight gives the debarment 0, because FLAG_WEIGHTS has no sanction, debar or wanted terms and only 'regulatory' has a fallback. The resignation (1) leads, and severity is never compared.
findings.fix: Give category sanctions weight 5 and regulatory 4 before the title is read. Add bar and sanction events to FLAG_WEIGHTS, and break ties on SEVERITY_WEIGHT before sourceAuthority. Add mdb-debarment, us-bank-regulators, fincen-actions, delaware-courts, eu-courts, canada-federal-courts and us-agency-orders to PRIMARY_SOURCES so the authority's record leads its matter.
findings.evidence: Jest repro: redFlags order was [web-search medium resignation, mdb-debarment high].
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. A tied, high-severity mdb-debarment flag (category 'sanctions') sorted below a medium resignation. FLAG_WEIGHTS has no bar, debar or sanction terms, the category fallback covers only 'regulatory', and severity is never compared when sorting red flags.

findings.title: Coverage text contradicts the screens: Delaware 'not covered' after it ran; partial sources unmentioned
findings.scenario: In r9, delaware-courts answered 3 lookups (clear), yet notCovered says 'Court dockets (CourtListener is not enabled...), including US state courts and the Delaware Court of Chancery'. us-agency-orders, federal-register and us-lobbying show 'partial' in screens, but partlyAnswered ignores s.partial, so the brief's gaps section is silent about them. Web archive's 3 failed lookups out of 25 are not mentioned either.
findings.fix: Drop the Delaware clause when delaware-courts answered. Include sources with s.partial in partlyAnswered (reason: 'parts did not answer: ...'). List every failed lookup count under 20% as a one-line note, not nothing.
findings.evidence: Jest repro and r9 brief: the notCovered[0] string, and screens us-agency-orders 'partial' absent from GAPS.
findings.verifyNote: notCoveredFor adds the Delaware Court of Chancery clause whenever court-dockets is silent, without checking delaware-courts. partlyAnswered checks only errors at 20% or more and waitedOut, never s.partial; my run showed uk-gazette 'partial' missing from partlyAnswered. Failed lookups under 20% never reach the brief.
findings.betterFix: Also add s.partial and failures under 20% to coverage.searched rows, so that cleanScreens and the brief read one source of truth.

findings.title: Name-only noise is numbered ahead of every record about the person
findings.scenario: score() weighs severity x3 over match x2, so a possible medium item (9) outranks a confirmed info one (7). In r9, #2-#7 are the RAMP & CO LTD liquidation, 'Body found near ... Boat Ramp', and 'The Ramp church ... abused two minors', all ahead of #9 onward. Hacker News 'Ramp-Up' (#134-#136), placeholder text (r8 #37/#38) and a people-search-style bio site (#137) are kept too.
findings.fix: Rank tied records first: sort by match tier (confirmed/likely, company, possible), then score. Drop records with data.companyNamesake that name neither the person nor the company as a name. Drop pages whose snippet advertises age, net worth or marital status (people-search style), and template placeholder text.
findings.evidence: Jest repro: four possible records numbered 1-5 before the confirmed one. r9 sources #5 and #7.
findings.verifyNote: score() gives severity x3 against match x2: a possible medium press record scores 6+2+1=9 and a confirmed info one 0+6+1=7, so name-only noise is numbered first. Sorting by match tier first is consistent with rule 2. Dropping people-search pages is consistent with the privacy rule, though those hosts should already be blocked in guardrails.
findings.betterFix: Sort tied records (confirmed, likely, company) before possible ones, then by score. Do not drop companyNamesake records outright. Move them to a collapsed 'name only' group at the end, which keeps coverage honest.

findings.title: One page is counted 3-11 times, which inflates totals; archived copies and own posts lose their tie
findings.scenario: r8: merge.dev is #3/#13/#20, forbes #5/#6/#16/#21, accel #10/#15/#22, plus #37/#38 graded possible. The substack page is #14/#26. The bottom line says '26 tied' but there are about 10 pages. r9 has 11 copies of the Fortune pieces, and 'Gil Feig' lists 13 records. Her own post x.com/shensi/status/... (#44) is 'possible'.
findings.fix: Canonicalise URLs: strip the web.archive.org prefix and www, resolve page-reader and search duplicates. Group them as one record with alsoIn, and give the group its strongest tie. A URL under a trusted profile URL (x.com/shensi/...) is at least likely. Count totals per page.
findings.evidence: r8 sections archive, career, press and identity listings; r8 #44 url https://x.com/shensi/status/2123466322440818768 has match possible.
findings.verifyNote: In deepCheck, pageKey is urlKey plus the headline of the title, so one URL found under different titles (search result vs page reader) is kept twice. urlKey does not strip the web.archive.org/web/<ts>/ prefix, and archive records are exempt from URL dedupe. The report adds no URL grouping. I did not check the r8/r9 counts.
findings.betterFix: Fix this mainly in deepCheck.js: drop the title from pageKey for non-archive records, unwrap archive replay URLs in urlKey, and merge copies into alsoIn while keeping the strongest match (upgradeKept). In the report, count totals per canonical page. Raise a URL under a trusted profile URL to likely only if it is the same platform handle and the record names the person.

findings.title: Timeline is archive capture dates and a 1994 domain; real career events are missing
findings.scenario: In r9, 39 of 47 timeline rows are 'page as of' or 'archived N times' captures, and the first event is 'ramp.com: registered 1994-03-14' (a domain bought later). Paribus founded 2014, acquired by Capital One 2016, Ramp founded March 2019 and Harvard 2012 are absent. In r8, 8 of 9 rows are captures.
findings.fix: Exclude archive snapshot and summary records (data.kind !== 'change') from the timeline. Put a domain registered before the company's founding year as 'domain first registered (earlier owner)', off the timeline and out of WHAT CHECKS OUT. Add dated events read from tied quotes (founded/joined/graduated/acquired + year) with their cites.
findings.evidence: r9 timeline dump: 1994-03-14 n=103 first, followed mostly by archive rows.
findings.verifyNote: The `rest` filter includes category 'archive' with no data.kind check, so 'snapshot' capture records fill the timeline. domains.js gives the corporate record the registration date as its date, so a 1994 domain registration becomes the first event. No code reads dated career events from tied quotes.

findings.title: One liquidation is shown as three 'possible namesake' matters
findings.scenario: In r9, the UK Gazette notices #2, #3 and #4 (Appointment of Liquidators, Notices to Creditors, Resolutions for Winding-up) for RAMP & CO LTD on 2024-07-23 are three entries under 'Possible namesakes' and three 'Rule out' bullets in the brief. Name-only grouping needs 2 shared headline words and Jaccard 0.4, and these headlines share none.
findings.fix: In matterKey, group register and gazette records by the legal company name in the record plus the date (or within 14 days), before headline matching. Use the notice company from the title or quote, normalised.
findings.evidence: r9 possibleNamesake list: n=2, 3, 4, each with more=[].
findings.verifyNote: For 'possible' records, matterKey and agreement need at least 2 shared headline words and Jaccard 0.4. Event words such as liquidat and winding-up, and the company name in `skip`, are removed, so three notices about one company on one date stay separate. This is cosmetic: they stay with the possible namesakes either way.
findings.betterFix: For uk-gazette and fr-bodacc, key the matter on the notice's company name (from data, or title or quote) plus a date within 14 days, before headline matching.

findings.title: Real company news demoted to 'not clearly this company'
findings.scenario: In r9, #6 'After a failed partnership, Ramp's backers lobbied Washington to probe rival Airwallex's China ties' (Dealroom, The Information) is about Ramp. BUSINESS lacks backers, rival, partnership, lobbied and fintech-peer words, so ordinaryWordOnly marks it possible and it lands with the possible namesakes.
findings.fix: Widen BUSINESS (backers, rival, partnership, lobby*, competitor, deal, acquisition, payments, card, expense, Series, round). Treat the possessive or capitalised company word followed by a business noun as a name. Also accept a known peer company name (from tied records) in the same text.
findings.evidence: r9 #6 matchReasons: 'the word "Ramp" appears, but not clearly as this company'. Jest repro reproduced match=possible.
findings.verifyNote: BUSINESS lacks backers, rival, partnership, lobbying and competitor, so a headline about Ramp's backers fails BUSINESS.test unless the quote has a listed word, and is marked as a companyNamesake. Widening the list is safe because PART_OF_LONGER still catches 'boat ramp' and 'The Ramp church'.
findings.betterFix: Widen BUSINESS, but keep 'deal', 'card' and 'payments' out unless next to the company word: they are common in unrelated news. Treating the possessive form ('Ramp's') followed by a business noun as a name is a good signal.

findings.title: Without a model, profile and 'What checks out' drop the LinkedIn and Crunchbase facts the records hold
findings.scenario: In r9, archived Crunchbase and LinkedIn records state 'Co-Founder, CEO, Paribus (2014 - Feb 2019)', 'Harvard University (2008 - 2012)' and 'BA, Economics'. The profile shows Harvard only, with degree null (hard-coded), and earlier: []. WHAT CHECKS OUT lists ABS-15G and domain records instead. byEmployer cannot then raise the BrokerCheck Credit Suisse record (r8 #29), the Capital One patent (#124) or RAMP BUSINESS UK LTD (#115).
findings.fix: Parse the 'Experience:' and 'Education:' fields of tied profile snippets and archives into roles (with years), education (with degree and field) and founded. Pass degree and field through reportProfile. Build WHAT CHECKS OUT from profile lines backed by an independent record. Let byEmployer also use the legal names in confirmed filings (Form D issuer).
findings.evidence: r9 profile: earlier [], education degree null. Quotes in r9 #106 and #34.
findings.verifyNote: The proposed fix is partly already there: profile.js lines 244-255 already parse 'Experience:' and 'Education:' when the record title names the person. But years are stripped, reportProfile hard-codes degree and field as null and founded as [], and WHAT CHECKS OUT is built from category lists rather than profile lines. Archived LinkedIn records whose title does not name the person are skipped.
findings.betterFix: Extend the existing profile.js parser instead of writing a new one: keep years, degree and field (archiveClaims already returns education.degree and dates, so use data from archive records), and pass them through reportProfile. Raising byEmployer from Form D legal names is a separate item; keep its two-record rule for serious items.

findings.title: An interviewer's Substack is listed as the founder's profile link
findings.scenario: In r8, a trusted thread 'https://notanotherceo.substack.com' ('substack profile') appears, and the Profile card lists it as Shensi Ding's link. It is David Politis's newsletter. profileFromUrl maps any article URL on a substack.com subdomain to a profile of that subdomain.
findings.fix: For Substack (and medium.com/@), return a profile only for the root URL, never for /p/ article paths. In profile.js links, include a profile only when handleFitsSubject(subject, handle) or when the link came from the person's own Person node sameAs.
findings.evidence: profileFromUrl('https://notanotherceo.substack.com/p/shensi-ding-merge-74') returned {platform:'substack', handle:'notanotherceo'}. r8 profile.links includes it.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed in sources/web.js line 260, not in extract.js: when the result title names the person, profileFromUrl's url thread is added with no handleFitsSubject check. For Substack that thread is the root subdomain (notanotherceo.substack.com) of an article page. profile.js then lists it as their 'substack' link. threadsFromResult in extract.js itself does check handleFitsSubject.
findings.betterFix: In web.js, and in profileFromUrl for substack or medium, return a profile only for a root or about path, never for /p/ or article paths, and require handleFitsSubject unless the link came from the person's own Person-node sameAs. In profile.js links, apply handleFitsSubject to any platform whose URL carries a handle.

findings.title: Caps cut records without telling the reader
findings.scenario: The timeline slices at 60, capWikiOther drops articles from the report and its totals, and the quoted brief keeps 14 red flags, 8 company matters, 10 checks, 10 claim changes, 10 related parties, 8 namesakes and 5 possible changes. writeDeepBrief sends 12 company matters. None of these says how many were left out, so a 15th red flag disappears from the brief.
findings.fix: Return omitted counts (timelineOmitted, wikiOtherDropped) in the report. In quotedDeepBrief, append '… and N more [see report]' after every slice. Tell the model 'N more company matters not shown'.
findings.evidence: report.js lines 159, 627, 794 and 803-808 use slice() with no remainder text.
findings.verifyNote: These slices are visible in the code: slice(0,14) red flags, 8 company matters, 10 checks, 10 claim changes, 10 related parties, 8 and 5 in the gaps section, timeline 60, capWikiOther, and 12 company matters sent to the model. None reports how many were left out. Saying so is required by the honest-coverage rule (rule 5).
